A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SafeDiffCon research work. All 24 pages in each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–I, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original control and safety evaluations on Burgers’ equation, incompressible fluid and tokamak simulation tasks in Section 5, plus timing, ablation and sensitivity results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix B, including benchmark comparisons, inference timing, component ablations and parameter sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same uncertainty quantile, reweighted post-training loss, guided sampling and inference-time fine-tuning. The model architectures also match.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Burgers’ equation, incompressible-fluid smoke control and tokamak simulation tasks. The represented datasets and test scenarios in Sections 5.1–5.3 and Appendices F–H are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains BC, BC-Safe, PID, SL-Lag, MPC-Lag, CDT and TREBI. Comparator membership also matches within the fluid, tokamak and inference-time comparisons in Tables 2, 3 and 5.

E3.justification: Safety thresholds, evaluation metrics, solver-based evaluation procedures, dataset splits in Table 11, and training and sampling settings in Tables 12–20 are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the component ablations in Tables 4, 6 and 7, parameter sensitivity analyses in Tables 8–10, and qualitative control examples in Appendix C. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both retain the same conformal uncertainty calculations and experimental reporting practices. Neither supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, empirical error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout Tables 1–10 and Figures 2–5. For example, SafeDiffCon’s objective values remain 0.0011, -0.3548 and 0.0094 in Tables 1–3, with zero reported unsafe rates.

T1.justification: Theorems 4.1–4.3, their assumptions and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. The PDE formulations, conformal definitions and mathematical derivations also match.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning conformal adaptation, satisfaction of safety constraints and superior control performance. No claim is broadened or narrowed.

C2.justification: The interpretations of component effectiveness and baseline failures are unchanged, including Appendix I’s comparison caveats. Section 6 retains the same applicability discussion, future extensions and safety-accuracy tradeoff.

D1.justification: Appendices E–I retain identical implementation instructions and hyperparameters. Appendix B.1 retains the A800-with-eight-CPUs timing context, and the code-access URL is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list and the positioning relative to diffusion control, safe offline reinforcement learning and conformal prediction match. No cited work or novelty relationship changes.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 15 May 2025 to v4 dated 24 June 2026. Apart from spacing differences, the body wording, section order and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Small spacing and typesetting differences appear, including in the captions of Tables 8 and 20. Figures 1–5, table structures, caption wording and placement are retained; the embedded figure images match.

improvement.justification: v4 preserves the same methods, theoretical arguments, experimental evidence, limitations and reproducibility information as v2, including the appendices. The updated version stamp and slight typesetting differences do not materially improve or diminish the paper’s clarity or scientific support.
